comment.comment:
I genuinely think people are underthinking what is happening with AMC right now. This isn’t just “lol AMC token.” AMC might accidentally be the perfect asset for the first real GME of crypto.

Think about the lore. AMC is literally one of the stocks that defined the last retail rebellion. Reddit apes, hedge funds, shorts, CNBC, Robinhood, Adam Aron — the entire internet knows the story already.

Now fast forward 5 years. Robinhood is trying to put the financial system onchain, AMC gets tokenized, LONG launches a meme paired with AMC, Adam Aron notices and starts publicly freaking out about Robinhood tokenizing AMC, then Vlad responds.

Like bro. The AMC CEO and Robinhood CEO are now publicly arguing over the exact thing crypto has talked about for years: who controls financial assets once they move onchain?

You could not manufacture better lore. AMC dev vs Vlad. TradFi vs crypto. 2021 apes vs 2026 onchain degenerates. Except this time crypto has actual financial rails.

That’s the part people aren’t getting. Imagine CT actually adopts AMC as its stock. Not “we made another dog coin.” An actual public company becomes the meme.

Every new token pairs against AMC. Every trade routes attention/liquidity toward AMC. Every CT account starts posting the stock. Then Reddit notices again. Then AMC apes notice crypto bidding their bags. Then TradFi notices AMC getting relentless demand. Then shorts start asking who the hell is buying this thing.

The answer is literally: crypto.

That is where this gets schizo. What if this becomes the first stock where the crypto community essentially says, “Fine. We’re buying the company.”

5% ownership. 10%. 20%. Imagine an onchain ecosystem eventually controlling a massive chunk of the actual float.

Now every AMC shareholder watches crypto. Every crypto trader watches AMC. Every short watches both. Every Adam Aron tweet becomes crypto content. Every Vlad tweet becomes AMC content. Reddit and CT merge into one massive feedback loop.

Price creates attention. Attention creates memes. Memes create volume. Volume creates fees. Fees buy more stock. Stock goes up. Shorts feel pain. That creates headlines. Headlines bring more people in.

Reflexivity on top of reflexivity.

The original meme-stock trade was Reddit discovering that coordinated internet capital could fuss with Wall Street.

This version is crazier. Crypto already has 24/7 markets, global liquidity, memecoins, bots, launchpads, leverage and an entire culture built around turning narratives into billions.

Now point that machine at a real stock.

That’s the Robinhood Chain killer app. Not TPS. Not another lending protocol. Not “RWAs are the future.”

Show people an actual public company getting absorbed into crypto culture in real time.

The funniest possible ending is also the most bullish narrative: TradFi spends years asking whether crypto belongs in finance.

Then crypto just buys TradFi.
